A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HuSCF-GAN research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated complexity analysis and renumbered experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation and downstream classification experiments, simulated latency comparisons, component ablations, and additional PFL-GAN comparisons in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds medical-image, CIFAR10/SVHN, AudioMNIST, and genetic-algorithm experiments.

M1.justification: The cGAN architecture, split-training procedure, clustering, and KLD weighting remain unchanged. However, v1 describes reducing clients while preserving device proportions, whereas v2 specifies optimization over unique device profiles. Section 4.3 and Appendix D do not establish whether this changes the earlier reduction procedure or clarifies an incompletely documented implementation.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, KMNIST, and NotMNIST experiments, v2 evaluates BloodMNIST and DermaMNIST medical images, CIFAR10 and SVHN RGB images, and AudioMNIST spoken digits. These substantially broaden the represented domains and modalities. The illustrative assistant use case and proposed LLM extensions are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The evaluated GAN comparators remain FedGAN, MD-GAN, Federated Split GANs, PFL-GAN, and HFL-GAN, including in the added domains. The label-based KLD and additional PFL-GAN comparisons are retained. Appendix D quantifies the reduced-versus-full-search comparison already mentioned in v1 Section 4.3; the newly cited security methods are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces FID evaluation for CIFAR10/SVHN, audio preprocessing into 128-bin log-mel spectrograms resized to 28×28 grayscale images, GA parameter sweeps, and a 100-device reduction comparison. Section 6.1.5 also changes the number of clients missing three labels from 20 to 30 per domain. Its table estimates remain unchanged, so this establishes a revised reported setting without establishing that the experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The original component ablation, activation-versus-label KLD analysis, and PFL-GAN supplementary tests are retained. New Appendix B tests sensitivity to GA population size, crossover rate, and mutation rate. Appendix D adds quantified latency and convergence comparisons for profile-based versus client-based optimization, extending v1's brief 20-device validation statement.

E5.justification: v1 reports classification point estimates without uncertainty intervals. v2 introduces 95% Wald confidence intervals throughout the main and appendix classification tables. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting, but neither additional independent runs nor seed-based variability estimates are established.

E6.justification: Retained classification point estimates and the principal latency comparison are unchanged. Substantial new results include HuSCF-GAN accuracies of 63.67% on CIFAR10, 73.35% on SVHN, and 98.05% on AudioMNIST, plus medical-image and FID results. Table 27 reports 7.8 seconds and 12 generations for profile-based GA versus 8.26 seconds and 488 generations for client-based GA.

T1.justification: The original latency, aggregation, and computational-complexity mathematics is retained, with the latter relocated and renotated. Section 6.4.2 adds client/server space-complexity bounds. Appendix D states synchrony and identical-profile assumptions and argues for solution preservation, but supplies no formal proof of that assertion.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains heterogeneous split training combined with clustered, KLD-weighted federation under data-sharing constraints. The abstract and conclusion strengthen quantitative claims: maximum classification gains rise from 50% to 60%, generation-score gains from 2.2× to 3×, and a new claim of 2×–70× lower FID is introduced.

C2.justification: New Section 7 substantially expands limitations and interpretation, covering central-server dependence, reconstruction and label-inference vulnerabilities, optimization overhead, and tuning difficulties. v2 also discusses profiling assumptions, asynchronous operation, and audio-resolution limitations. Security mitigations and extensions to other architectures are prospective proposals, not demonstrated capabilities.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies GA crossover and mutation rates of 0.7 and 0.01, explains profile-based reduction, and documents the Librosa spectrogram pipeline. Existing architecture and device-capability tables are retained. Conversely, v1's code-availability statement and repository URL disappear; the PDFs do not establish whether the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: Although the original distributed-GAN related-work discussion is largely retained, v2 substantially expands positioning against split-learning attacks and defenses, including Pasquini et al., Shabbir et al., and encryption, differential-privacy, and detection approaches. It also adds references supporting the new datasets, FID, audio processing, and prospective architectural extensions.

P1.justification: Most existing introductory, background, methodological, and experimental prose is retained. Changes include targeted abstract and setup revisions, moving computational complexity from Appendix C into Section 6.4, introducing a dedicated Discussion section, and reorganizing appendices. Much of the expansion documents new scientific content rather than extensively rewriting the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds procedure, profile-reduction, and split-learning diagrams in Figures 5–7; expands the dataset example panel; and adds medical-image and FID plots. New result, memory-complexity, and GA-analysis tables substantially expand the displays. Existing classification tables accommodate confidence intervals, and complexity tables receive explanatory annotations and relocation.

improvement.justification: The added domain evaluations, GA analyses, memory bounds, and explicit privacy limitations improve support and transparency beyond v1's MNIST-focused evidence. These gains are limited by the removed code-access information and inconsistent new performance claims: Table 12 shows PFL-GAN outperforming HuSCF-GAN on DermaMNIST precision and F1 despite the broad superiority statement, while Figure 16 does not substantiate the advertised 70-fold FID reduction.
